summary: The change moves renderer workspace RPC to a shared, ticket-authenticated WebSocket. It keeps HTTP for file transfers, for prompt submission and, after the round-1 fix, for the initial compatibility probe. F1 is fixed: the review coverage plumbing and the Vite toggle are gone. F2 is fixed: the HTTP probe reports older servers as incompatible, and a temp regression with a real HTTP server covers it. The only blocker is the coverage gate: createHaloClient.ts:75, 116, 133 and HaloSocket.ts:17 are reported as uncovered, although the temp tests clearly run them.

testRequests.target: packages/client/src/createHaloClient.ts:75, :116, :133 and packages/client/src/HaloSocket.ts:17 (reported uncovered; the coverage gate fails)
testRequests.rationale: These lines run in every WebSocket client test. Line 75 constructs the HaloSocket, line 116 is inside the socket-link interceptor, line 133 closes the link object, and line 17 is the `socket` field of HaloSocket. Round 1 did not list them as executable. They appeared only after the Playwright temp test webHost.e2e.test.ts was added; its Node-side transform probably maps zero-count ranges onto these lines. Resolve this in one of two ways. Preferred: move the WebHost temp test into a vitest temp test, such as packages/workspace-server/test/.tmp-tests/, using the same real control plane and workspace, and rerun so these lines are counted as covered. Otherwise, add `coverage-exempt` reasons that name this mapping artifact and the tests that run the lines. I will accept those reasons.
